test_title: PYST 12: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - General Intelligence (Held On 24 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: reasoning
question:
Three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All figs are twigs.

Some twigs are trees.

Some ants are trees

**Conclusions:**

I. Some ants are twigs.

II. Some trees are figs.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d40877129b40e8a855d221c69e941b94524fc0b089217cc8e03397f92cb4cdd8.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some ants are twigs → **Does not** follow (As all figs are twigs, some twigs are trees and some ants are trees. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some trees are figs → Does not follow (As all figs are twigs and some twigs are trees. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion I nor II follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2"
